mainTopic: Whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי even in a ברייתא, when a torn ספר תורה sheet may be sewn and still be כשר, and the proper layout and rolling of a מזוזה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רבי חנינא's rule that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי applies wherever he taught, not only in our משנה. It then turns to a tear in the parchment of a ספר תורה. רב rules that a tear running into two lines may be sewn, but one running into three lines may not. רבא limits the three-line rule to 'old' parchment, which the גמרא explains means parchment not processed with gall, and the sewing must be done with sinew, not thread. רב יהודה בר אבא's question about a tear between columns or between lines stays unresolved (תיקו). The גמרא then turns to the layout of a מזוזה: lines of two words each are כשרה, and uneven lines of two, three and one are also כשרה, as long as the shape is not a 'tent' or a 'tail'. רב חסדא places ״על הארץ״ alone on the last line, with two views on where in that line it goes. Finally רבי חלבו reports how רב הונא rolled a מזוזה and wrote its sections סתומות, and the גמרא begins a challenge from a ברייתא about רבי מאיר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule covers every place he taught, not only our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier challenge. רבי חנינא never limited his rule to our משנה. He said 'any place where he taught,' so it includes ברייתות too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he say 'in our משנה'? He said 'any place where he taught'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering an earlier objection. It points out that רבי חנינא's rule about רבי שמעון שזורי was worded broadly, so it also covers a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed the rule 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי' applies only to what he taught in the משנה. The answer reads רבי חנינא's exact words: 'כל מקום ששנה', any place he taught. That wording covers ברייתות as well, so the objection falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the official collection edited by רבי יהודה הנשיא
Any place where he taught, meaning wherever his teaching appears
'Did he say...?' A rhetorical question meaning 'he did not say that'

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי applies wherever he taught, in the משנה or in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Does he say 'in our Mishnah'?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי חנינא, who said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.

phrases.english: He says 'any place where he taught.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an objection raised just before this passage, about whether רבי חנינא's rule covers ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the original statement's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule might apply only to רבי שמעון שזורי's teachings in our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies wherever he taught, including ברייתות.

steps.title: A tear of two lines may be sewn, but not a tear of three
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through רב חננאל and רב זעירא, rules on a tear in a ספר תורה. If it runs into two lines, it may be sewn. If it runs into three lines, it may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זעירא said that רב חננאל said that רב said: A tear that runs into two lines may be sewn. If it runs into three, it may not be sewn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with רב's basic rule about fixing a torn sheet of a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small tear crossing two lines can be fixed by sewing, and the scroll stays כשר. Once the tear reaches three lines, sewing does not fix it. The number of lines the tear crosses is what decides the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A tear, here in the parchment of a ספר תורה
Lines of writing
He may sew it, so the scroll can be fixed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא, אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ze'eira said that Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
A tear that runs into two lines may be sewn,
into three lines, it may not be sewn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְעֵירָא, אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tear crossing two lines may be sewn and the scroll stays כשר. A tear crossing three lines may not be sewn to make it כשר.

steps.title: The three-line rule applies only to old parchment
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטי tells רב אשי a teaching of רבא. The rule against sewing a three-line tear applies only to 'old' parchment, not to 'new' parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטי said to רב אשי: This is what רבי ירמיה מדיפתי said in the name of רבא. When we said 'three lines, do not sew,' we meant only old sheets. With new sheets, we have no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא limits רב's rule from step 2. A three-line tear cannot be sewn only on 'old' parchment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 sounded like a rule for every parchment. רבא narrows it: on 'new' parchment, even a three-line tear may be sewn. Step 4 will explain what 'old' and 'new' mean.

keyTerms.meaning: Old ones, meaning old sheets of parchment
New ones, meaning new sheets of parchment
We have no problem with it, so it is allowed
We only said this about..., a phrase that limits an earlier rule

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטֵי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabba Zuti said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִדִּיפְתִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said in the name of Rava:
That which we say, 'into three lines, it may not be sewn,'
we said only about old sheets,
but with new sheets, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמְרִינַן ״בְּשָׁלֹשׁ אַל יִתְפּוֹר״ לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּעַתִּיקָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's three-line rule from step 2 to old parchment only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-line tear may not be sewn only on old parchment. On new parchment it may be sewn.

steps.title: What 'old' and 'new' really mean, and sewing with sinew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'old' and 'new' do not refer to age. 'Old' means parchment not processed with gall, and 'new' means parchment that was. It adds that sewing fixes the tear only when done with sinew, not with thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Old' does not literally mean old, and 'new' does not literally mean new. Rather, 'old' is parchment not processed with gall, and 'new' is parchment processed with gall. And this applies only to sewing with sinew, but with thread, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words 'old' and 'new' from step 3. It then adds a condition about what material the sewing must use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is about how the parchment was processed, not how long ago it was made. Parchment processed with gall (אפיצן) counts as 'new' and may be sewn even with a three-line tear. Parchment that was not processed counts as 'old.' The sewing must also be done with sinew (גידין). Thread (גרדין) does not make the scroll כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, actually
Processed with gall, a tanning treatment for parchment
And this statement applies only..., a phrase that limits a rule
Sinews, the animal tendons used for sewing ספרי תורה
Threads, such as ordinary flax thread

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'old' and 'new' as describing age. A brand-new sheet that was never processed with gall still counts as 'old' here.
steps.whatToRemember: A tear of up to two lines may always be sewn. A three-line tear may be sewn only on parchment processed with gall. In every case the sewing must be with sinew, not thread.

phrases.english: And 'old' is not literally old,
and 'new' is not literally new,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּלָא אֲפִיצָן, הָא דַּאֲפִיצָן,
phrases.english: rather, this is parchment not processed with gall, and that is parchment processed with gall,
phrases.notes: The first one, not processed, is the 'old' sheet. The second one, processed, is the 'new' sheet.

phrases.english: and this applies only to sewing with sinew,
but with thread, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the terms used in step 3 and adds a condition about the sewing material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Old' means not processed with gall and 'new' means processed with gall. Sewing makes the scroll כשר only when done with sinew, not thread.

steps.title: What about a tear between columns or between lines?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אבא asks what the הלכה is when the tear is not through the writing itself. It might run in the blank space between columns, or between lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אבא asked: If the tear is between one column and the next, or between one line and the next, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised about tears that fall in the blank spaces of the scroll. The גמרא is setting up the next step, where we learn whether it was answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule counts how many lines of writing a tear crosses. A tear in the empty space between columns, or running between lines, does not cut through writing in the same way. So it is unclear whether the line-counting rule applies there.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, used for a real question whose answer is not known
A column of writing in the scroll
A line of writing
What? Asking what the law is

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Abba asked:
Between one column and another column,
phrases.notes: He means a tear in the blank space between columns that is as long as a tear of more than three lines would be.

phrases.english: between one line and another line, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Here the tear runs sideways in the gap between two lines, without cutting through letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the tear rules and asks about tears outside the written area.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the three-line rule apply to a tear between columns, or to one running between lines?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question of רב יהודה בר אבא stands without a decision.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question by saying it stays undecided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source or argument could settle the question. The law for a tear between columns or between lines is left open in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The law for a tear between columns or between lines is left undecided (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question of step 5 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about tears between columns or between lines is left unresolved.

steps.title: A מזוזה written two words per line is כשרה
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through רב חננאל and רבי זעירי, rules that a מזוזה written with two words on each line is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירי said that רב חננאל said that רב said: A מזוזה written with two words on each line is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב about the layout of a מזוזה. Even very short lines, just two words each, are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same chain of teachers as the ruling about the torn ספר תורה, now speaking about a מזוזה. It shows that a מזוזה does not need long, full lines to be כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The parchment with the פרשיות of שמע and והיה אם שמוע, fixed on a doorpost
Two by two, meaning two words on each line
Valid, kosher for use

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירִי, אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ze'eiri said that Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
A mezuzah that one wrote two by two is kosher.
phrases.notes: "Two by two" means only two words on each line of the parchment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירִי, אָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same chain of teachers as step 2, but a new subject: the layout of a מזוזה instead of a tear in a ספר תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה written two words per line is כשרה.

steps.title: What about uneven lines of two, three, and one words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a מזוזה is כשרה if the lines are uneven: two words, then three, then one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If the lines are two words, then three, then one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רב's ruling, and sets up the answer that comes next. Even lines of two are fine, but what if the lines are all different lengths?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allowed short lines when they were all the same length. The new question is whether uneven, mixed lengths are also allowed, or whether the lines must at least match each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them; an open question the scholars were unsure about
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Two, and three, and one, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means two words on one line, three on the next, and one on the line after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב's case of even short lines to uneven lines.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a מזוזה with uneven line lengths (two, three, one) כשרה?

steps.title: Uneven lines are surely כשרה, like a song
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that uneven lines are certainly כשרה, since this makes the מזוזה look like a שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: All the more so it is כשרה, since he made it like a שירה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. Uneven lines are not only allowed, they are even more clearly fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that uneven lines look like the special 'song' layout used for שירת הים in the Torah. Since that is a respected layout, using it in a מזוזה should surely be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; even more clearly
A song in the Torah, like שירת הים, written in a special layout of uneven lines

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
All the more so, since he made it like a song.
phrases.notes: The "song" is like שירת הים in a ספר תורה, which is written in lines of uneven length.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ כְּשִׁירָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Uneven lines are certainly כשרה, because the מזוזה then looks like a שירה.

steps.title: A teaching says writing it like a song makes it invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק from a ברייתא that says writing it like a שירה makes it פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a teaching: If he made it like a song, or made a song like it, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of רב נחמן בר יצחק. Writing in a song layout makes it invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק used the song layout as a reason to allow uneven lines. The ברייתא says that switching layouts, writing regular text like a song or a song like regular text, makes it פסולה. That seems to knock out his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it like a song, using the song layout for regular text
Invalid, not kosher

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂאָהּ כְּשִׁירָה, אוֹ שִׁירָה כְּמוֹתָהּ – פְּסוּלָה!
phrases.english: If he made it like a song, or a song like it, it is invalid!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling that a song layout makes the מזוזה even more clearly כשרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that using a song layout for regular text makes it פסולה, the opposite of his claim.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is speaking about a ספר תורה, not a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to a ספר תורה. For a מזוזה, the song layout is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a ספר תורה, each part must be written in its own proper layout, so mixing them up makes it פסולה. A מזוזה does not have that rule, so רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scroll
That one, meaning that ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The same layout can be פסולה in a ספר תורה but כשרה in a מזוזה. The rule depends on which item you are writing.

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was about a Torah scroll.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a different case (ספר תורה, not מזוזה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא invalidates a song layout everywhere, including in a מזוזה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא applies only to a ספר תורה; in a מזוזה the song layout is כשרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also allows uneven lines, with two limits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling supports the view that uneven lines are כשרה, as long as the lines don't steadily grow longer or steadily get shorter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן (and some say it was רב אחא בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן): A מזוזה made with two, three, and one words per line is כשרה, as long as he doesn't make it like a tent, and as long as he doesn't make it like a tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא's ruling that agrees with רב נחמן בר יצחק. It also adds two shapes that are not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן confirms that uneven lines are כשרה. But mixed lengths are not the same as a steady pattern. Lines that keep getting longer (a 'tent') or keep getting shorter (a 'tail') are excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated; a support from another אמורא
Provided that, only if
A tent; lines that steadily get longer
A tail; lines that steadily get shorter

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה may have uneven lines (two, three, one), but not lines that steadily grow (a tent) or steadily shrink (a tail).

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Acha bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מְזוּזָה שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ וְאַחַת – כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: A mezuzah that one made two, and three, and one is kosher,
provided that he does not make it like a tent,
phrases.notes: A "tent" shape means the lines get wider as you go down: one word, then two, then three.

phrases.english: and provided that he does not make it like a tail.
phrases.notes: A "tail" is the reverse: the lines keep shrinking, three words, then two, then one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of steps 9 and 11 and adds limits.
steps.raayaObject: That uneven lines (two, three, one) in a מזוזה are כשרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling, as reported by רבה בר בר חנה or רב אחא בר בר חנה.

steps.title: ״על הארץ״ goes on the last line, end or beginning
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the closing words ״על הארץ״ are written on the last line. Some say at the end of the line, and some say at the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: 'Upon the earth' goes on the last line. Some say at the end of the line, and some say at the beginning of the line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about where the last two words of the מזוזה go. It also reports a disagreement about their exact place on that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that ״על הארץ״ sits on its own final line. The argument is only about where on that line: at the end, or at the start.

keyTerms.meaning: "Upon the earth", the last two words of the מזוזה
The last line

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
"Upon the earth" is on the last line,
phrases.notes: These are the very last words of the מזוזה: דברים 11:21.

phrases.english: some say: at the end of the line,
and some say: at the beginning of the line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: ״עַל הָאָרֶץ״ בְּשִׁיטָה אַחֲרוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new layout rule for the מזוזה, about the closing words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״על הארץ״ is written alone on the last line; the views split on end or beginning of that line.

steps.title: Why each view places ״על הארץ״ where it does
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two views. Each one reads ״כימי השמים על הארץ״ differently, and places ״על הארץ״ to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says at the end of the line reads it like 'as the heavens are high above the earth.' And the one who says at the beginning of the line reads it as: just as the heavens are far from the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each view from step 13. Each view comes from a different picture of the heavens and the earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view pictures heaven right above the earth, so ״על הארץ״ goes at the end of the last line, directly under ״השמים״ at the end of the line before. The other view stresses how far heaven is from earth, so ״על הארץ״ goes at the start of the line, far from ״השמים״.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says; introduces the reason of one view
The heavens are high, from the פסוק in תהלים
Is far away, distant

steps.whatToRemember: Both views put ״על הארץ״ alone on the last line. They differ only on end versus beginning: right under ״השמים״ (heaven above earth) or far from it (heaven distant from earth).

phrases.english: The one who says at the end of the line,
is like "as the heavens are high above the earth,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:11. At the end of the line, ״על הארץ״ sits right below ״השמים״ on the line above.

phrases.english: and the one who says at the beginning of the line,
is just as the heavens are far from the earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the two views in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: End of line: heaven directly above earth (תהלים 103:11). Beginning of line: heaven far from earth.

steps.title: How רב הונא rolled and laid out a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו testifies that רב הונא rolled the מזוזה from "אחד" toward "שמע" and wrote its sections סתומות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said: I saw רב הונא roll the מזוזה starting from the word "אחד" toward the word "שמע". He also wrote its sections in the closed style.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an eyewitness report from רבי חלבו about two things רב הונא did when he made a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first detail is about rolling: he rolled it from the end of the first פסוק back toward the beginning, so that "שמע" ends up on the outside. The second detail is about layout: he made the two sections סתומות, meaning closed, not open.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolls up or wraps
Toward
Sections (here, the two sections written in a מזוזה)
Closed: the new section starts on the same line where the last one ended

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said:
I saw Rav Huna
that he would roll it from "Echad" toward "Shema",
phrases.notes: "שמע" is the first word of the מזוזה and "אחד" ends that first פסוק, so he rolled from the end back toward the start (דברים 6:4).

phrases.english: and he would make its sections closed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where ״על הארץ״ is written (Steps 13-14) to two new details about making a מזוזה: how it is rolled and whether its sections are open or closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה is rolled from "אחד" toward "שמע", and its sections are written סתומות, based on רב הונא's practice.

steps.title: Beginning a challenge from how רבי מאיר wrote a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to challenge רב הונא's practice from a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר describes how רבי מאיר wrote a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that רבי מאיר used to write the מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס, shaped like a column of a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב הונא's practice. It begins quoting a ברייתא about how רבי מאיר wrote a מזוזה, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא only tells us two things: the material (דוכסוסטוס) and the shape (a tall, narrow column). The actual clash with רב הונא has not come up yet. It will appear when the rest of the ברייתא is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of hide (the inner layer of the animal skin) used for writing
Like, a kind of
Here: a column, like a column of a ספר תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the contradiction in these words alone. The ברייתא is cut off here, and the part that actually challenges רב הונא comes next.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Rabbi Meir would write it
on dukhsustos, like a kind of column,
phrases.notes: "Column" means tall and narrow, like one column in a ספר תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against the practice of רב הונא reported in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's practice as reported by רבי חלבו (Step 15)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's way of writing a מזוזה, as described in the ברייתא, is being set against רב הונא's practice. The specific point of conflict comes in the continuation of the ברייתא.
